title: Sunset Boulevard
events_chronological: Joe Gillis, a screenwriter three months behind on his payments, is dodging the finance men who want his car back.
Joe pitches a baseball picture at Paramount and a young reader named Betty Schaefer tells the producer to his face that it is flat.
Running from the finance men, Joe blows a tyre and swings into the drive of a derelict mansion on Sunset Boulevard.
Joe is taken for the undertaker come to collect a dead chimpanzee and meets Norma Desmond, a silent star nobody has thought about in twenty years.
Norma hires Joe to cut the enormous script she has written for herself about Salome.
Joe moves into the room above the garage, and the butler Max collects his things from his flat without asking him.
Norma buys Joe suits, a cigarette case and a watch, and the arrangement quietly becomes a kept one.
At a New Year's Eve party laid on for two, Norma tells Joe she is in love with him, and Joe walks out to a friend's party instead.
Max telephones to say Norma has cut her wrists, and Joe comes back and stays.
Joe begins slipping out at night to write a script with Betty Schaefer, who is engaged to his friend Artie.
Norma drives to Paramount with the Salome script; Cecil B. DeMille is gentle with her, and Joe learns the studio only ever wanted to hire her car.
Max admits that he directed Norma's first pictures, that he was her first husband, and that he has been writing her fan mail himself for years.
Norma telephones Betty, and Joe brings Betty to the house and tells her exactly what he is, to make her leave.
Joe packs, tells Norma the truth about her career and the letters, and walks out towards the pool.
Norma shoots Joe three times and he falls face down into the swimming pool.
With the police and the newsreel cameras filling the hall, Norma takes them for a film crew and comes down the staircase ready for her close-up.
syuzhet_notes: The film opens on the body floating in the pool and on the dead man's own narration, then rewinds six months and runs forward until it arrives back at the same water. Only that one scene is displaced; everything else is in order.
fabula_notes: The narrator is dead throughout, but the narration is voice-over rather than a scene the story is told from, so the body in the pool is a genuine flash-forward rather than a frame.
